subject.title: [Feature]:  Missing Session Management Commands in OpenClaw

question: Which session lifecycle slice should OpenClaw expose first for this broad request: a safe stop/abort UI and CLI, a hard-kill child-process boundary, pause/resume semantics, or quota/resource-limit policy?
rationale: Current code has partial primitives but no single safe product contract for hard-kill, pause/resume, UI control, and quotas; choosing the API semantics and security boundary needs maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Scope an MVP stop/delete surface
options.body: Expose clear CLI and Sessions UI controls around existing `sessions.abort` and strengthened `sessions.delete`, while leaving hard-kill, pause/resume, and quotas to narrower follow-up issues.

options.title: Prioritize hard-kill semantics
options.body: Use #12554 as the canonical first milestone and design process-tree termination and child exec ownership before adding broad UI affordances.

options.title: Design the full lifecycle model first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers specify stop, kill, pause, resume, cleanup, and quota semantics together across Gateway, CLI, UI, and agent tools.

recommendation.title: Scope an MVP stop/delete surface
recommendation.body: Expose clear CLI and Sessions UI controls around existing `sessions.abort` and strengthened `sessions.delete`, while leaving hard-kill, pause/resume, and quotas to narrower follow-up issues.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent and heavy session gateway/CLI history makes this the best available routing owner for choosing the first safe lifecycle slice.
